items.rationale: The frame sustained theft damage, so §§7.1.7(b) and 7.1.9 cover a like-for-like replacement. The estimated €260 gross is reduced to €130 by the shared €500 mobility limit (§4.2.2).
The brakes were damaged in the theft, so §7.1.7(b) covers equivalent parts. The estimated €139 gross is reduced to €70 by the shared mobility limit.
The tracker helped locate the bicycle, but no theft or damage to the tracker itself is established. Sections 4.2.3 and 7.1.5 exclude its replacement.
The second bicycle was unaffected, and routine servicing is independently excluded under §§3.1.6 and 7.1.5.
Neither accessory is shown to have been stolen or damaged. Sections 3.1.7 and 4.2.3 exclude these supplementary purchases.

Section 7.1.7(f) covers necessary carriage of the damaged bicycle or its repair parts, not shipping for unrelated purchases. If allocated to the covered repair, €25 gross becomes €12.50 under the shared mobility limit.

No separate necessary repair attendance is established; §§7.1.8(f)–(g) and 7.1.10 exclude unsupported or duplicate charges. If a distinct covered visit is substantiated, €30 gross would reduce to about €15.

Section 7.1.7(c) covers necessary fitting of the replacement frame and brakes, excluding any service work or labour billed twice. The estimated €140 gross reduces to €70 under the shared mobility limit.
Sections 7.1.7(e) and 7.1.10 allow only sundries consumed in the covered repair; the generic description leaves the allocation uncertain. An €8 covered allowance reduces to €4.
Section 7.1.7(d) covers separate apprentice labour needed for the theft repair, but not servicing or work already included in assembly. One eligible hour at €18 gross reduces to €9.
Section 7.1.7(d) covers necessary skilled repair time to the extent it is distinct from the assembly charge and second-bike service. One eligible hour at €39 gross reduces to €19.50.
The initial attendance was needed to release the recovered bicycle and is independently covered by §5.2.2(a). The estimated €32 gross reduces to €16 under the shared mobility limit.

items.description: Cutting and removal of seized lock
items.rationale: Section 5.2.2(b) covers cutting and removing the fastening needed to release the bicycle. The estimated €100 gross for the two units reduces to €50 under the shared mobility limit.

Sections 5.2.2(a) and 7.1.8(f) cover a return attendance only if it was needed for recovery; the description establishes no such need after release. If substantiated, a €32 gross visit would reduce to about €16.

items.description: Mandatory impound release and storage fee
items.rationale: The yard required payment before releasing the bicycle, so §5.2.2(c) covers €100 plus 19% VAT. The €1,000 recovery limit does not bind, but the shared €500 mobility limit reduces €119 to €60.
Sections 3.1.5 and 7.1.8(d) exclude claim-processing charges. This is distinct from the yard's mandatory release fee.
Section 5.2.2(b) covers apprentice time actually used to release the bicycle, provided it is not already billed in the lock-removal line. One eligible hour at €18 gross reduces to €9.
Section 5.2.2(b) covers necessary skilled release labour, subject to the duplicate-cost rule in §7.1.8(g). One eligible hour at €39 gross reduces to €19.50.
